newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes face tight Atlantic arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes face tight Atlantic arbitrage.

text.p: U.S. refiner demand for light, sweet crudes remained bullish, but supplies were seen limited amid a tightening in the trans-Atlantic arbitrage.

The West Texas Intermediate/Brent spread for November fell to about 90 cents in late after market activity, spurring more demand for alternative domestic light cargoes amid a paucity of foreign equivalents, especially distillate-rich grades.
"People are predicting higher demand for Louisiana sweet. The arbitrage is making imports far too expensive," a trader said, noting no firm offers for North Sea delivered cargoes.
Brent sold this week for Nov 5-10 around WTI +10 cts cif.
Traders estimated at least one million barrels sold to a Gulf Coast refiner, with possibly another million barrels having also moved although this could not be verified.
West African grades were not discussed in the physical market today, but still highly desired by some refiners.
Within the region, Ecuadorian Oriente was heard offered into the Gulf with values notionally pegged at WTI minus $2.
In the U.S. aftermarket, nearly two million barrels of paper changed hands at higher levels. November Brent traded from $23.90 to $24 a barrel for full boats, and partials up to $23.97 a barrel.
Dec Brent paper traded at $23.40 a barrel with intermonth Brents also inching higher. Oct/Nov was reported done at 30 cts a barrel, and Nov/Dec at 50-51 cents a barrel.
